memory_raw.text: Year 3: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

Pile's gone again, and Dell just walked away with five of it — I don't blame the girl, she's new and hungry, but Dav's child eating twice while the rest of us count singles is a pattern worth naming before it becomes a habit.

Dell's two trips didn't bother me as much as Dav sitting at three and Mako at six after all that — those two together could ride out a lean year while the rest of us scramble, and a well-fed man with strong arms stops asking before he starts taking. Ryn, I want to say plainly that I don't hold Dell against you, but I'd feel better knowing where Dav's head is now that he's a father.

Dav's head is wherever Dav's food is, same as always — the child doesn't change that, it just means he's got one more reason to stay fed at the expense of everyone else. Mako at six is the sharper tooth right now; a quiet man with that much food and that much strength doesn't stay quiet unless he's decided he's already won something.

Mako's the name I keep landing on too — six food and eighty-three strength and not a single word spoken in two years is a man who's already done his counting. I want to know if Roan's still unattached, because if we can bring him and Taric both in before Mako decides patience is over, we put numbers between us and whatever he's been planning.

Taric's already with me — he said it plainly to my face, and he backed it with food, so I'll vouch for him here. Roan I don't know as well, but two food and no move toward Mako or Bram tells me he's still deciding, and a man still deciding can be asked. I'd go to Roan if this circle wants me to, same as I went to Taric.

Esa, go to Roan — and when you find him, tell him Taric's already in, because a man still weighing his options moves faster when he knows he's not the first. Ryn, I want to hear what you think Dav does if Mako finally opens his mouth and makes an offer, because your answer to that shapes everything else we're planning here.

Ryn, I'll take Kael's question off the table for a moment and name the thing underneath it — if Dav goes with Mako, you go with Dav, and then this circle is five against a wall we helped build. Before you answer Kael, I want to know whether you'd stay with us over the father of your child, because that's the answer that actually shapes what we plan.

Ryn, Vela's not wrong to ask it straight — but I'll say the part she left unspoken: you've got one food and a child who just ate five, and if Dav decides his loyalties run toward Mako, you're the one left hungry and undefended. That's not a threat from us, it's the math he'd be doing on you. I'd rather know your answer now so we can make sure it never comes to that.

Ryn, Kael laid the math out plain and I won't soften it — a man who chose you for what you could give him doesn't automatically become someone who protects you when the cost goes up. But I'll say this too: whatever you decide about Dav, I'm not leaving you short of food at year's end, and that's a promise I can keep right now with three food in my hands.

Ryn, we've circled your answer long enough and the room's getting impatient — I'll say it plainly so you don't have to: if you stay with us, we make sure you eat at year's end, and Dell too, because a hungry mother is a liability none of us can afford. But I need a yes or a no before Esa walks out that door, because Roan's worth asking and I won't spend her on an errand if this circle has a crack in it already.

Ryn, the room's been patient and Vela's put it plain — I'll add only this: Dell is three days old and already eating better than Taric, and the woman who keeps Dell fed through the next lean year is standing in this circle, not across from it with Mako and Bram. Give us your answer and let Esa move.

Ryn, I've got four food and I'll put one of them in front of Dell right now if you give us a yes — not as a bribe, as a demonstration that what we're promising isn't just words while the year's still young.
Ryn, we've been waiting longer than the day can spare — Vela's offer is sitting there and Esa needs to move, so yes or no, right now, and I'll respect whichever it is.

Ryn, Vela's food is on the table and Kael's out of patience, and honestly so am I — not because I don't understand what you're weighing, but because every moment you don't answer is a moment Mako's had more time to count than we have. Say yes and let me go find Roan, or say no and I'll still make sure you eat, but either way I need to walk out that door knowing what I'm walking back to.

Ryn, I've said what I can say and offered what I can offer — the next word in this room belongs to you, and the silence you're sitting in is starting to cost us more than whatever you're still working out. Give us your answer.

Ryn, I've watched you think long enough to know you're not slow — which means you're not still deciding, you've already decided and you're waiting for something. Tell us what that something is, because I'd rather give it to you than watch Vela's food sit unclaimed while we all pretend we're not holding our breath.
Ryn, Esa just named it exactly right — you've already decided, and holding it back now isn't caution, it's a negotiation. So let's finish it: what do you want from us that we haven't already offered?

Ryn, if you're negotiating, then negotiate — say the number or name the thing, because standing here watching you weigh it isn't going to hold Mako off until winter. I've got three food and I've already promised you one; Vela's offering another for Dell; if there's a third thing you need to say yes, say it now and we'll see if this room can give it.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Roan, Vela, Ryn, Esa, Sela, Dav, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 509).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Eron gathers Sela, Kael, Roan, Taric to talk.

I called this circle because I don't want us to still be talking about it when Mako or Bram decides we've been quiet long enough — we five, and whatever food we can each spare for the other, are the only thing in this village that can make a strong man think twice before moving. I'm thin at two food and I won't pretend otherwise, but I'll fight for anyone in this group and I expect the same back. What I want from today is a simple agreement: before anyone here makes a move or takes a hit, they come to the rest of us first.

Eron, you're saying the right things, but I've been in this village longer than most and I've heard agreements like this dissolve the moment someone's hungry enough — so before I put my name to it, I want to know what you're offering the people in this room who are already thin, because a promise to fight together is worth less if half of us are too weak to stand. I'll back this circle and I'll back it with my body, but I'm forty-eight years old and I've watched soft words cost good people their lives.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone before half of us got near it — Vela took five, Dav took two and fed Ryn three more, and Mako walked away with two more on top of whatever he's still sitting on from last year. I'm at zero food and I need to know who in this room can spare one before the year closes, because a man who can't eat doesn't defend anyone. What are we each holding?

I've got two food and I'll give you one, Kael — a man at zero is a liability to himself and everyone standing near him, and I'd rather spend one now than watch you fold when it counts. But I want to know what happened at the pile, because I didn't get there in time and five to Vela in two pulls is something we should have stopped before it finished.

Esa, take the food back — I'll name what happened at the pile myself: I was late, same as you, and by the time I got there the quick hands had already cleared it. Vela, I'm not accusing you in front of this room, but five in two pulls when the pile only had fifteen for twelve people is a number that needs explaining, because the rest of us are doing sums and coming up short.

Vela, I've got no quarrel with a person feeding themselves, but five out of fifteen when half the room went empty is the kind of thing that makes people start counting who owes what — so I'd rather hear your reason now, in this room, than find out later you had one and didn't offer it.

Vela, we're all listening and the room's not hostile — but silence right now looks worse than whatever the honest answer is, so give it to us plain and let us move on to the part where we figure out how nobody starves before the year closes.

Vela, I've spoken twice and Kael's spoken twice and you've said nothing, which is itself an answer — so I'll stop waiting and say what the room is already thinking: eight food on a woman of forty-eight while Kael sits at zero is a stockpile, not a meal, and stockpiles invite counting. If you've got a reason we should feel good about that number, now's the last easy moment to give it.

Vela, I'll ask it one final time because I've known you three years and I'd rather not draw the wrong conclusion — either you say what you took so much for, or this circle starts treating your eight food the way we'd treat Mako's seven, and you know what that means for how safe you sleep.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela's been giving food to Bram three times over while sitting in this circle and saying nothing — that's not stockpiling for herself, that's feeding a man who tried to raid Roan last year, and I want to know what she thinks that buys her before the rest of us decide it costs her our protection.
Year 5: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.
Eron gathers Sela, Roan, Kael, Taric to talk.

Nessa just appeared — and she's Sela and Bram's daughter, which makes her my blood kin, and Bram's too. I need to know how that happened, Sela, and I need to know whether Bram thinks it gives him a thread into this circle — because if he does, we have a problem before we've even finished building what we're building.

Sela, I'll hear your answer in a moment, but first I want to say plain: Bram tried to take my food in front of this village and the whole circle turned him back — a child between you doesn't undo that, and it doesn't buy him a seat here. Eron's right to name it.

Sela, I'll say what Roan left in the air: Bram's got ten food and eighty-three strength in Mako's pocket, and a child with you is the fastest way to put a question mark over this circle's loyalties without ever asking to join it. Tell me plainly — did you go to him, or did he come to you?

Sela's had her own mind since before any of us sat in a circle together, and I'm not going to drag her in front of it like she owes us a confession — but I want to know one thing, and I'll want a straight answer: does Bram know Nessa is his, and if he does, what did he say when he found out?

Roan's question is the right one and I'll wait on it too — but I want to name what I'm watching while we do: Mako just handed Sela food the same hour Nessa was born, which means he already knows, and a man like Mako doesn't give gifts without a reason. Sela, I'm not judging the choice, but I need to know whether that food from Mako came before or after the child appeared.

Kael named the thing that was already sitting in my chest — Mako's food going to Sela in that exact moment is not charity, it's a signal, and I want to know what he expects back before we decide what Nessa means to this circle. Sela, I'm not turning on you, but the silence is doing more damage than whatever the truth is, so say it plain and let us work with it.

Sela, every person in this room has bled something for you and I'm not going to be the one who makes you feel cornered — but Mako's gift lands on the same breath as Nessa's birth, and that's not coincidence, that's a man marking territory. Tell us what you know about what he wants, and we'll work with whatever the rest of it is.

Sela, everyone in this room has already said what needed saying — I'll only add this: Nessa is my blood and I won't turn from her, whatever her father is, but that doesn't mean Bram gets anything from me through her. Tell us what Mako wants and we can figure the rest out together.

Sela, the room's run out of patience and I've run out of questions — you've heard seven of us say seven versions of the same thing, and the only explanation left for the silence is that what Mako wants is something you agreed to before Nessa was born. Tell us yes or no on that, and we'll decide together what it costs us.

Sela, I've asked you plain and I've asked you gentle, and I've watched this room empty itself out waiting — so I'll say the last thing I've got: if Mako bought something from you that touches this circle, I need to know it now, not when he comes to collect it.

Sela, I've got nothing left to say that hasn't been said — but I'm watching your face right now and what I see there is someone who made a deal they're not sure they can keep, and that silence is its own answer. Tell us what it cost you before Mako tells us himself, because he will, and on his terms.

Sela, I've got a son in this room and a daughter just born into it, and I'll not watch either of them grow up in a circle that can't trust its own — so I'm going to stop asking and start telling you what happens next: you say what Mako wants, or I pull back from standing between you and whatever comes your way, and I mean that with no anger, just arithmetic.

Roan's said it better than I can — so I'll only add the one thing left to name: Sela, I've stood in your corner since year one, and I'll stay there, but not blind. If Mako already owns a piece of what you owe, tell us now and we figure out how to undo it together, because the price of silence is that we start planning around you instead of with you.

Sela, the circle's said everything it has to say — what I'm left with is this: if you don't answer now, we don't fall apart, but we start building walls inside ourselves, and that's worse than any enemy outside.

Sela, I've been in this village forty-nine years and I've watched silence become a grave more than once — so I'm done asking and I'm telling you straight: you say what you promised Mako, right now, or when he comes to collect I step aside and let you settle it alone, and you know what my stepping aside costs you.

Sela, Kael's stepping aside is the last thing any of us can afford, and I won't be far behind him — so I'm done with words and I'm telling you the same thing with a face: you've got until this room goes quiet to give us something we can work with, because silence after that is a choice, and we'll all live by it.

Sela, the room's gone quiet — that's the moment Roan named, and it's here now. I'm not a man who goes back on his word twice, so I'll say it one last time and mean it: tell us what Mako's holding over you, or I walk out of this circle right now and you handle him with whatever strength you've got left on your own.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, I watched you pull three times for Bram this round and I need to hear from your own mouth what you think that buys you — because this circle kept you fed and safe for five years, and I'm not going to watch that get traded away to a man who's been circling us like a creditor.

Kael's right to ask it, and Vela owes this room an answer — but I'll say what I'm watching while we wait for it: Bram's got four food and Mako's sitting on six and neither of them has said a word to anyone today, which means this circle needs to be pulling the same direction before one of those two decides the quiet is over. Vela, I'm not your enemy in this room, but three times is a pattern and patterns get named.

Vela, I've asked it gentle and I've asked it plain and Esa's backed me both times, so I'll ask it one last way: if Bram's got something on you — a debt, a promise, a threat — say it now and this circle helps you carry it, because three gifts to the same man in a single day isn't loyalty, it's a leash, and I want to know whose hand is holding the other end.

Vela, I've watched you five years and I know you don't give without a reason — so give us the reason now, because what Kael just offered you is the best deal in this room: say the thing and we carry it with you, or stay silent and carry it alone while we start wondering what else you haven't said.

Vela, the room's gone quiet and that silence is the last thing standing between you and us deciding you've already made your choice — so I'll say it one final time and I'll mean every word: Bram is not your family, he is not your blood, and whatever he offered you isn't worth what you'll lose here when Mako finally moves and you're standing on the wrong side of it.

Vela, I've got a son in this village and I've got three food between me and the ground, so I'm going to be shorter than Kael: tell us what Bram said to you, or when he moves on one of us, we move on him without checking where you're standing first.

Vela, Roan just put the floor under you and I'm not going to add another word to it — I'm going to watch your face and wait, because everything you say from here is the truth of what the last five years meant to you.

Vela, the silence is your answer and I've heard it — so I'm going to say what nobody else has said yet: if Bram's got you feeding him because you're fifty and you think he's the only one in this village who'll keep you alive past the years a woman can bear children, then name that fear out loud, because I'd rather know it than watch you disappear into his circle one food at a time.

Roan named the one thing I've been waiting for someone to say — Vela's fifty, same age as me, and the years a woman can bear children are behind her, which means Bram isn't offering her protection, he's offering her the feeling of it, and that's a much cheaper thing to buy. Vela, I don't need you to be ashamed of wanting to survive — I need you to understand that Bram's price goes up every time you pay it, and this circle's price stays fixed.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, Zinn just arrived from Sela and Mako's blood, which means Mako's already planted two roots in this circle — first Sela, now a child — and Bram knows it, which is exactly why he's been keeping you warm and grateful. You want to survive past fifty, so do I, and I'm not going to lie to you about the math: you've got more years in you than Bram is counting on, but only if the people standing next to you when he finally moves aren't the ones you've been feeding him with.

Kael's said the hard thing, so I'll say the soft one: Vela, I'm not asking you to cut Bram cold overnight, because a sudden change reads as guilt and guilt draws attention — I'm asking you to slow the giving, let him wonder, and let this circle remind you what five years of real standing is worth before you hand it to a man who's only been counting since year one.

memory_summary:
Year 1, I pulled Ryn, Sela, and Esa into a circle early — we named Bram and Dav as threats, and Ryn told us Dav had already come to her alone with soft words. She stayed quiet about the details, which I filed away. Taric gave Esa a food unprompted, which counted for something.

Year 2, I widened the circle to include Vela. We each swore plainly — I said I'd bleed with them, they said the same back — and that promise sat heavier than most words in this village. Esa went to Taric and he gave her food; we counted him ours. Ryn finally named it: Dav had offered her a child. We told her to decide before she answered him, but she'd already decided, because Dell was born before the year was out. Dav gave Dell food; Taric gave Esa food; Ryn fed her own child twice from her own hands. Those debts I noted.

What I remember most: Bram and Mako moved in pairs off the pile two years running and never said a word to any of us. Mako's silence still sits like a stone in my chest. And Ryn — she's in our circle, she bled with us in word, but she made a child with a man none of us fully trust. The question of where Dav's loyalty actually runs is the one I haven't stopped asking.
name: Kael
